memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "'Meat that touches anything ceremonially unclean must not be eaten; it must be burned up. As for other meat, anyone ceremonially clean may eat it.'" - Lev 7:19 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The meat was holy. It had been offered to God, blessed, set apart. And a single contact with something unclean ruined it entirely.

That tells us something about how contamination worked in the old system. Holiness was fragile; uncleanness was aggressive. One touch was enough.

This is exactly why the old covenant could never finally solve the problem. Its holiness had to be constantly defended and could be lost in a moment. Israel lived permanently on the edge of defilement.

Then Jesus came, and the direction reversed. He touched lepers, dead bodies, and bleeding women — every category of uncleanness — and never once contracted it. Cleanness flowed out of Him instead.

Hebrews explains why this matters: The blood of goats and bulls... sanctify them so that they are outwardly clean. How much more, then, will the blood of Christ... cleanse our consciences (Heb 9:13-14). External cleansing was fragile. Internal cleansing is not.

The holiness God gives you in Christ is not a delicate thing you might accidentally lose by contact with the wrong person or place. It is Christ's own righteousness credited to you.

You do not have to live afraid of contamination. You are held.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do I live as though my standing with God is fragile and easily lost?
2. What difference does it make that Christ's cleansing works from the inside out?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, thank You that my holiness in Christ is not fragile. Free me from anxious living and settle me in what He has done. Amen.
